title: Seed datasets cannot carry a file: a `Field.file` column needs a `sys_file` id only an upload can mint, so a declarative seed either drops the row, breaks the ADR-0104 attestation, or inserts a dangling token silently
body:
Blocked-by: #25692

Filing class: ③ platform gap, filed at destination from an app ruling. Reader: `domain:server` / `area:records` seed + storage triage. Unlabelled, no assignee. Origin: objectstack-ai/hotclm#19, ruled **D** by the maintainer on 2026-10-25 (ruling comment https://github.com/objectstack-ai/hotclm/issues/19#issuecomment-6396327991): "the platform's seed loader should carry bundled fixture files; the app keeps `file` required".

## Context

hotclm's `clm_contract_version.file` is `Field.file({ required: true, storage: { notNull: true } })` (a version without its document is not a version), and its design asks for 300 seeded versions so the demo shows a negotiation timeline with counterparty redlines. A `file` value is an opaque `sys_file` id; the bytes live in the storage backend under the row's `key`. A declarative seed has no upload and cannot mint one. The same wall stands in front of `clm_contract_type.template_file`, `clm_signature.executed_file`, `clm_obligation.evidence`, and in this repo's own showcase (#4891: an image column seeded with a data: URI blocks the ADR-0104 attestation).

## Measured (17.3.0, sqlite; premise re-checked on hotclm main 2026-10-25 — field unchanged, loader unchanged)

One seed load, three version rows differing only in `file`:

1. `file` omitted → `ERROR [SeedLoader] Failed to write clm_contract_version record #2 … File is required`; the whole row is lost.
2. `file` is a URL → the row inserts, then `WARN [migration] NOT attesting 'adr-0104-file-references' … Expected an opaque sys_file id`.
3. `file` is an id-shaped token (`probe-file-token-0001`) → inserts **silently**, no warning, reads back verbatim, download 404s. ⚠️ This third shape is the one a seed could "get away with" and is itself a gap: nothing validates that a seeded `sys_file` reference exists.

Consequence in the app: zero seeded versions, `version_count` reads 0 on all 120 contracts, the version timeline is empty, and the ten seeded drafts cannot be submitted (the `draft → submitted` guard wants a version file or a type with a template, and the seed can supply neither).

## The gap

`packages/runtime/src/seed-loader.ts` and the dataset schema in `packages/spec/src/data` have no notion of a file column: no way to point a seed value at bytes the package ships, and no check that a seeded `sys_file` id resolves.

## What is asked

1. A seed-time file reference, shape the platform's to choose, e.g. `file: seedFile('fixtures/nda-v1.pdf')` (or `{ $file: 'fixtures/nda-v1.pdf', contentType: 'application/pdf' }`) in a dataset record: the loader writes the bytes to the storage backend, mints the `sys_file` row with the (object, record, field) ownership the platform already enforces for uploads, and stores the id in the column; idempotent across boots (content hash or the dataset's identity key); the fixture path resolved relative to the package so both locales produce identical rows. 300 rows may reference the same bundled file (the platform copies bytes per owner today).
2. The loader refuses an id-shaped `sys_file` value that does not resolve (closes shape 3 above), or at least warns loudly, the same way the ADR-0104 migration refuses shape 2.

Cross-app pull: HotCRM attachments on accounts/opportunities, the showcase's images (#4891), hotsrm supplier documents.

## Dedupe

`search_issues` on this repo for seed + file / sys_file / fixture documents: #22149, #19672, #4704, #15262, #9308, #9070, #4891, #3415 — seed identity, env, replay and showcase problems; **0** about seeding file columns.

## Not asked

- No relaxing of `required` on app file fields to accommodate seeds (hotclm option C, rejected by the maintainer).
- No runtime upload inside the app's demo script (hotclm option B, rejected: the seed must stay declarative). hotclm#19 is `Blocked-by` this card and ships 0 versions until it lands.
